Operating Conditions, Safety and Durability for Class VIII Vehicles Report : At the start of the program, as per task 2, requirements and operating conditions for the LH2 tank were gathered. These flow from the operating conditions of the truck and safety requirements for the tank on the truck. Many public-domain reports from various agencies such as US-DOT, UN, EU, ISO and ANL covering both these aspects were accessed and the critical information was collected and compiled into a report. Aspects such as truck life, fatigue loading, thermo-mechanical loading, crash safety, fire safety and durability requirements were collated into this report. One observation to be made is that public-domain information on standards, safety and durability are generally 10 to 20 years old, also, and not comprehensive. Hence, the compiled report is not considered comprehensive and needs to be updated. This report [6] was submitted to DOE in Q4, 2024. 8. UDRI: Material and laminate testing under ambient and cryogenic conditions: UDRI performed the fabrication and testing of coupons for mechanical and thermal response and for material properties at room temperature and cryogenic temperature. Composite test coupons were fabricated without and with carbon nanotubes (CNTs). The following sub-sections provide the details of the test set-up, testing and main test results. Further details are in a report by UDRI [7]. Page 20 of 30 Approved for Public Release 8.1. Introduction: Material evaluation through laminate level and coupon testing of carbon/epoxy laminates under cryogenic conditions was performed. A novel cryostat was designed for performing a variety of mechanical tests of polymer matrix composites (PMCs). Shear and tensile testing of various control and nano-modified laminates was conducted using the developed cryostat chamber. Room temperature and liquid nitrogen (LN2) test data on mechanical properties, including an assessment of the microcracking initiation (via acoustic emission) and extent of microcracking was evaluated using optical microscopy. Panels were fabricated as per manufacture’s guidelines, and after fabrication, panels were subjected to flash thermography (FT) scans to check for defects prior to testing. Additionally, the use of Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs) was proposed to reduce microcracking- a critical consideration in composite tanks. Carbon/Epoxy based cryogenic storage tanks can have microcracking (under repeated thermal cycling) which may lead to reduced structural integrity and leakage/permeability concerns. 8.2.
